key_insight: Engine position changes early contrail-vortex interactions and wake instability, but its influence fades as vortex dynamics and atmospheric conditions dominate later evolution.
engineering_relevance: For aircraft design and emissions mitigation, engine placement can affect initial contrail formation and near-field wake behavior, but it is not a strong long-term control on contrail microphysics in the studied cases.
method: 3D Large Eddy Simulations on a realistic aircraft geometry
Eulerian bulk microphysical model coupled to the flow solver
Initialized from prior RANS fields; tested 3 engine positions under 2 stratifications and 2 humidity levels
evidence_signal: The abstract reports consistent trends across multiple simulated configurations: engine position altered vortex descent, instability onset, and particle distribution, yet contrail properties converged over time.
watch_item: Results are limited to the modeled aircraft, atmospheric conditions, and parameter range studied, so the conclusions may not generalize to all engine layouts or weather states.
paper_title: Engine position effects on contrail evolution for a realistic aircraft configuration
